newsitem.title: USA: IMF team recommends it pay Russia loan tranche.
newsitem.headline: IMF team recommends it pay Russia loan tranche.

text.p: An International Monetary Fund team has recommended payment of the latest tranche of a $10 billion IMF loan to Russia, a fund official said on Wednesday.
Alexei Mozhin, the IMF's alternate executive director for Russia, told reporters a mission to Moscow had returned with a positive report on Russia's economic performance.
"The board has to approve the report of the mission which came back from Moscow. It was positive ... The day after the board approval, the money becomes available," Mozhin said.
He said the board meeting was expected on October 8.
Russia's three-year Extended Fund Facility loan is subject to strict monthly monitoring of economic performance criteria.
Mozhin said some talks on the latest tranche were held during this week's annual meetings of the IMF and World Bank.

Russian Finance Minister Alexander Livshits told a news conference that practically all finance ministers from the Group of Seven rich industrial nations had raised questions about the level of tax collection in Russia.
"The general opinion was that the central problem was to bring balance to the budget. If we ensure that, then we will be able to solve the other problems," Livshits said.
An earlier $330 million tranche of the loan was delayed due to IMF concern over tax collection and budget revenues.
Russian officials have said they are confident they can meet their performance criteria under the loan programme for the rest of the year.
